chunks: And it is narrated from Ḥamzah ibn Ḥumrān, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I enter the market intending to buy a bondwoman, but she says, 'I am free.'
He عليه السلام said: "Buy her unless she has evidence."

key_terms.اشْتَرِهَا: purchase her; an instruction permitting the transaction
key_terms.السُّوقَ: the marketplace where buying and selling takes place
key_terms.بَيِّنَةٌ: clear evidence or proof establishing a legal claim
key_terms.جَارِيَةً: a female bondwoman being considered for purchase
key_terms.حُرَّةٌ: a free woman, not subject to sale as property

ai.seo_question: Can a bondwoman's claim of freedom prevent her sale without proof?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the purchase of a female slave in the market when she claims to be free. The ruling is that her claim is not accepted on its own in a commercial setting unless she possesses clear evidence establishing her freedom.
